text:
alice: Customer (acct: org-672) reporting intermittent 502s + TLS timeouts hitting hosted inference in eu-west2 starting ~08:30 UTC. They say requests sometimes hang for ~10s then gateway returns 502. saw spike in errors: request_id=6c1f3b9a

support-bot: Escalation created: INC-2026-768. Customer provided logs and sample request ids. Attached user repro: curl --request POST 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate' -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","prompt":"hello"}' --header 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***'

infra-oncall: I'm looking at edge/gateway logs for eu-west2. Observing increased TLS renegotiation and multiple connections with "connection reset by peer" from some upstream nexthops. Not a code deploy. No config changes in control plane since yesterday.

ben: We rotated a transit peer with provider X at 06:00 UTC for capacity (no infra changes), might be related. Provider says no incidents but we saw some asymmetric paths. Can we get a traceroute from affected customer IPs?

simon: I asked OPS to run traceroute + tcpdump. I also ran a targeted traceroute from an internal probe to the VIP. Traceroute shows path that hits providerX -> providerY and then stalls when DF bit is set (possible PMTU issue). Output: ```traceroute to api.redwood.com (34.120.12.9), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.28 ms  0.23 ms  0.20 ms
 2  100.64.3.2  0.79 ms  0.81 ms  0.74 ms
 3  providerX-gw  12.9 ms  13.1 ms  12.8 ms
 4  providerY-peer  25.2 ms  25.1 ms  25.6 ms
 5  * * *  (DF set)
```

claire: That's suspicious — PMTU blackholes often show up when ICMP is filtered and fragmentation is blocked. If large TLS records can't get through, the connection stalls and ALB/gateway returns 502 after backend timeout. Any tcpdump showing "frag needed" or ICMP type 3?

juan: Captured a short pcap from the edge host. Snippet from tcpdump: ```12:34:56.789 IP 203.0.113.45.54321 > 34.120.12.9.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1457, ack 1, win 64240, length 1456
12:34:56.800 IP 34.120.12.9 > 203.0.113.45: ICMP 3/4 Fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu = 1400)
12:34:56.801 IP 34.120.12.9.443 > 203.0.113.45.54321: Flags [R.], seq 0, ack 0, win 0
```
 We do see ICMP type 3 code 4 from a hop but it seems intermittently dropped by provider path.

maya: Customer's client opens TLS with 16k TCP segment sizes (TLS records can be large). If PMTU discovery fails and ICMP unreachable is filtered, the TCP stack doesn't reduce MSS and retries with large segments -> stalls. This maps to their 10s hang before gateway tears down.

ben: Two actionable mitigations: 1) Apply MSS clamping on our egress/edge routers to lower TCP MSS to 1360 for that transit path (temporary). 2) BGP tweak: prepending or re-announce to nudge providerY to prefer direct path that supports MTU 1500. Which is lower risk?

infra-oncall: MSS clamping is quick and reversible — I'll patch the edge ACL/iptables on edge nodes for the affected nexthop and roll out to eu-west2 edge fleet with canary 10% first. Command we'll push: ```iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu``` Applying now to canary node rwd-eu1-edge-03.

alice: I told the customer we have a mitigation and to expect decreased 502s within 5-10 minutes after rollout. Asked them to share a failing request id if they still see it.

support-bot: Customer replied: "saw drop from 12% error rate to 1.2% after you changed something, thanks — will monitor." They also sent a new request id that succeeded which aligns with canary timeframe.

simon: After canary looks good, we'll push to remaining edge nodes in eu-west2. Also engaging providerX support to whitelist ICMP type3 on that transit leg. Raising ticket with providerY with pcap attached.

claire: Postmortem notes for later: - Root cause: PMTU blackhole due to transit path filtering ICMP frag-needed messages after a recent transit peer rotation. - Trigger: client TLS large records + DF set -> fragmentation needed -> ICMP blocked -> connection stalls -> gateway timeout -> 502s. - Detection: correlation of increased TLS reset/connection stalls and pcap showing ICMP type3 intermittently. - Mitigation: MSS clamping on edge (short term), request provider fix (long term), consider adding automated MSS clamp rule when traceroute + pcap patterns detected.

juan: Open PR in infra repo to add a toggleable MSS-clamp runbook + automated canary script: will link once created.

ben: Also add a monitoring alert for "ICMP frag-needed observed" (count of ICMP type3 code4) so we detect recurrence earlier.

alice: Customer confirmed 24 hours later: no recurrence. Marking incident resolved pending provider fix. Will follow up with vendor ticket ID.

infra-oncall: Post-incident action items assigned: (1) full rollout of MSS clamp in eu-west2 - done, (2) provider ticket & ICMP whitelist - open, (3) automation for detection - in progress.

support-bot: INC-2026-768 updated to resolved (status: monitoring).

alice: thanks team :thumbsup: Good write-up, we'll include this as a playbook entry for network-induced 502s.
